definitions.explanation: The protective case or sheath for a Japanese sword. An essential component of a complete sword mounting, traditionally made of wood with a lacquered finish.

examples.japanese: {刀鞘|かたなざや}から{刀|かたな}を{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: He drew the sword from its sheath.

examples.japanese: この{刀鞘|かたなざや}は{漆|うるし}で{美|うつく}しく{塗|ぬ}られている。
examples.english: This scabbard is beautifully coated with lacquer.

examples.japanese: {博物館|はくぶつかん}には{江戸時代|えどじだい}の{名工|めいこう}が{作|つく}った{刀鞘|かたなざや}のコレクションが{展示|てんじ}されている。
examples.english: The museum displays a collection of scabbards made by master craftsmen of the Edo period.

notes:
A compound of {刀|かたな} (sword) and {鞘|さや} (sheath). The {鞘|さや} is one of the key components of a Japanese sword's {拵|こしらえ} (mounting), along with the {柄|つか} (handle) and {鍔|つば} (guard).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {刀鞘|かたなざや}から{抜|ぬ}く: draw from the scabbard
- {刀鞘|かたなざや}に{納|おさ}める: sheathe (a sword)
- {漆塗|うるしぬ}りの{刀鞘|かたなざや}: lacquered scabbard

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鞘|さや}: sheath (general term, used alone for any sheath or scabbard)
- {拵|こしらえ}: sword mounting (the full set of fittings for a Japanese sword)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditional Japanese sword scabbards are made from {朴|ほお}の{木|き} (magnolia wood) and often finished with elaborate lacquerwork. Fine scabbards are considered works of art in their own right and are valued by collectors.
